topic: Human Physiology Part 2: Nervous, Endocrine, Excretory, and Skeletal System
description: This study guide provides a detailed overview of the vital systems responsible for control, coordination, waste removal, and the structural framework of the human body.

sections.title: Nervous System
sections.description: The system that controls and coordinates all voluntary and involuntary activities of the body.

key_concepts.explanation: It is the longest cell in the human body and serves as the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.
Comprises the Brain and Spinal Cord. It acts as the main information processing and control center of the body.
The largest and most developed part of the brain, responsible for controlling intelligence, memory, learning, and consciousness.

key_associations.extra_info: Coordinates voluntary muscle movements and maintains equilibrium.
Controls vital centers like heartbeat, blood pressure, and respiration.
Acts as the body's thermostat; also the center for hunger, thirst, and emotions.

important_facts.fact: The weight of an average adult human brain is approximately 1350 to 1400 grams.
The human body has 12 pairs of Cranial Nerves (arising from the brain) and 31 pairs of Spinal Nerves (arising from the spinal cord).

sections.title: Endocrine System
sections.description: A system of ductless glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream to regulate body growth, metabolism, and development.

key_concepts.explanation: Chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands in trace amounts that travel through the blood to specific target organs to produce a physiological response.

key_associations.extra_info: Known as the 'Master Gland' because it controls the functions of most other endocrine glands.
Requires iodine for synthesis; deficiency of dietary iodine leads to Goitre.
Regulates blood sugar levels; its deficiency causes Diabetes Mellitus.
Known as the 'Fight or Flight' hormone, preparing the body for emergency situations.

important_facts.fact: The Thyroid gland is the largest endocrine gland in the human body.
The Pineal gland secretes Melatonin, which regulates the circadian rhythm (sleep-wake cycle) or the body's internal biological clock.

sections.title: Excretory System
sections.description: The biological system responsible for the elimination of toxic nitrogenous waste products and maintaining osmoregulation.

key_concepts.explanation: A pair of bean-shaped main excretory organs that filter blood to form urine and maintain fluid balance.
The structural and functional microscopic unit of the kidney where actual blood filtration and urine formation occur.
An artificial medical process used to purify the blood and remove wastes when a patient's kidneys fail to function.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Filtration of blood plasma under high hydrostatic pressure in the Bowman's capsule of the nephron.
scientific_principles.application: This is the primary and most crucial step in the formation of urine.

important_facts.fact: The pale yellow color of normal human urine is due to the presence of a pigment called Urochrome (derived from hemoglobin breakdown).
Normal human urine is slightly acidic in nature, with an average pH of around 6.0.
Humans are 'Ureotelic' organisms, meaning their primary nitrogenous excretory waste product is Urea.

sections.title: Skeletal System
sections.description: The structural framework of bones and cartilages that provides shape, mechanical support, and protection to internal organs while facilitating movement.

key_concepts.explanation: A specialized, rigid connective tissue composed heavily of a mineralized matrix containing calcium and phosphorus salts.
A tough, elastic band of fibrous connective tissue that connects one bone to another bone at a joint.
A tough, inelastic band of fibrous connective tissue that connects a skeletal muscle to a bone.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the longest, largest, and heaviest bone in the human body.
It is the smallest and lightest bone in the human body.
It is the largest and strongest bone in the human face, and the only movable skull bone.

important_facts.fact: A normal adult human skeleton consists of 206 bones, whereas a newborn infant has approximately 300 bones (which fuse as they grow).
The human skull contains a total of 29 bones (8 cranial, 14 facial, 6 ear ossicles, and 1 hyoid bone).
The skeleton is divided into the Axial skeleton (80 bones forming the central axis: skull, ribs, sternum, spine) and the Appendicular skeleton (126 bones forming the limbs and girdles).
